messages:
Emma - Support: Hey team, ACME Ops opened a billing escalation — their invoice shows ~24% more tokens billed than tokens served according to their logs. Customer says this started after we flipped the continuous-batcher on for them earlier this month.
ACME Ops - Customer: Confirming. We see fewer served tokens in our app logs compared to the invoice. Example request ids: req_8a3f, req_8a7b.
Emma - Support: I dug up the tenant logs and saw a lot of prefetch/kv hits around those request ids. Not obvious why billed > served. Tagging eng infra.
Raj - Eng-ML: @Emma can you paste a sample request trace and the billing-meter line? Need to check if metering happens at submit time vs final served tokens.
Emma - Support: Pasted below (trimmed):
```
2026-02-18T10:12:34Z req=req_8a3f submit tokens=1200
2026-02-18T10:12:34Z batcher cbatch_id=cb-77 prefetch=true tokens_metered=1200
2026-02-18T10:12:34Z runtime kvcache HIT prefix=true served_tokens=300
2026-02-18T10:12:34Z response served_to_client tokens=300
```

Maria - Eng-Runtime: That pattern screams prefetch meter-before-serve. Continuous batcher issues prefetch candidates to warm KV cache and those prefetches are counted by the metering pipeline today. If the cache subsequently satisfies the main request, served tokens are less than what was billed.
Nora - Eng-SRE: Is prefetch performed as separate RPCs to the model? If so, billing picks it up as independent requests (we meter at RPC ingestion).
Raj - Eng-ML: Yes prefetchs are separate internal requests that generate token delta. Historically we assumed prefetch + main request ~ equivalent work, but with high cache hit rates we double-count.
Oliver - Finance: This is significant for customer invoices. ACME has been high-volume; 24% is material. We need a clear root cause and a remediation plan before we promise credits.
ACME Ops - Customer: We can share more request ids and a week of logs. We rolled cbatch on 2026-02-10.
Emma - Support: Created a repro pipeline that replays a subset of their traffic with cbatch on/off. Early results: cbatch ON -> metered tokens up 18-28% depending on warm-cache ratio.
Raj - Eng-ML: Thanks. Two immediate questions: 1) do prefetch requests have the same meter tags as customer requests? 2) are prefetches linked back to the original request id in billing exports?
Maria - Eng-Runtime: Prefetches are tagged as internal=true in tracing but metering pipeline currently ignores internal flag for token aggregation. We _do_ attach parent request id in debug logs but not in billing exports.
Nora - Eng-SRE: TL;DR: meter counts tokens at RPC arrival across the runtime; prefetches count today. We should have been excluding warmup-only prefetches from billing, but that logic never landed in the metering path after continuous-batcher rollout.
Oliver - Finance: If that's the case, customers with aggressive prefetching will see inflated bills. We need an immediate stop-gap and a long-term fix.
Emma - Support: ACME asking for credits for Feb 10-28. What do we recommend?
Raj - Eng-ML: Short-term options: 1) Backfill billing export to dedupe internal prefetch tokens by parent id (post-process) for affected time window, OR 2) Patch metering to ignore internal prefetch tokens going forward and issue credits for past delta.
Maria - Eng-Runtime: Backfill is feasible but expensive. Also we need to ensure we can reliably link prefetch RPCs to the final served request — sometimes prefetches are shared across multiple original requests in cbatch, which complicates attribution.
Nora - Eng-SRE: Also consider TTL-based prefetching: some of the prefetches that were billed were never consumed; those are purely warmup. We should exclude prefetches that don't have a downstream served trace within X seconds (say 5s).
ACME Ops - Customer: Attribution to parent request id would be ideal. We can accept credits for the delta if you can show reproducible reasoning.
Oliver - Finance: Let's not promise anything yet. We need exact numbers (credits $) and a safe stop-gap so this doesn't recur.
Emma - Support: Action items proposed: 1) Eng to produce a reproducible diff (cbatch ON vs OFF) with counts and sample ids (Raj/Maria). 2) SRE to propose stop-gap config to disable external metering of prefetches or tag them (Nora). 3) Finance to calculate provisional credit range (Oliver). 4) Support to coordinate with customer and collect full logs (Emma).
Raj - Eng-ML: I'll run a controlled replay this afternoon and produce CSV: request_id, submit_tokens, prefetch_tokens, served_tokens, metered_tokens. Will attach sample traces.
Maria - Eng-Runtime: For stop-gap I can flip a runtime featuregate to mark prefetch RPCs as "meter-exempt" before they hit metering pipeline. It's low-risk and revertable. Need approval and a quick rollout plan.
Nora - Eng-SRE: Approve featuregate rollout in canary first (one region), monitor metering delta, then global. I'll prepare runbook and SLO rollback.
Oliver - Finance: If we gate now and it stops billing new prefetches, that handles future invoices. For past invoices we'll need backfill/credit work. Please estimate delta and exposure by EOD.
Emma - Support: @ACME Ops can you DM me full logs and a primary contact? I'll open a formal support ticket TICKET-2026-197 and CC Finance.
ACME Ops - Customer: DM sent. We appreciate the quick triage.
Raj - Eng-ML: Reproducer results (summary): replayed 50k requests, cbatch ON => metered tokens 22% higher on average; cbatch OFF => metered ~= served. Raw CSV uploaded to internal bucket (link: https://redwood.internal/repro/cbatch-acme-0226.csv).
Maria - Eng-Runtime: I've prepared the featuregate PR that sets `runtime.prefetch.meter_exempt=true` and a metering-filter to drop/exclude tokens with that flag (will still emit metrics for observability). PR: https://git.redwood/runtime/pull/4521.
Nora - Eng-SRE: Deployed featuregate to canary region at 2026-02-27T22:05Z. Early telemetry: prefetch metered tokens in canary dropped by ~98% and end-user invoice-like aggregates dropped ~20% (matches repro). No errors.
Oliver - Finance: Based on canary and repro, provisional credit estimate for ACME (Feb 10-28) is $12,300 - $15,600. I'll formalize exact amount after we validate full logs.
Emma - Support: Finalizing ticket with timeline and proposed credit range. Will ask ACME if they want a partial immediate credit or wait until full backfill.
ACME Ops - Customer: Partial immediate credit would be appreciated. We can accept interim credit and reconcile later.
Emma - Support: Great. I'll propose interim credit at 75% of provisional estimate and update once backfill completes.
Raj - Eng-ML: Long-term fix: we should add dedup/attribution in billing exports and ensure internal=true prefetches are either filtered or attributed correctly. I'll scope design doc.
Maria - Eng-Runtime: Agreed. Also adding a small guard: prefetches that never produce downstream served traces within 5s get dropped from metering. I'll add to design.
Nora - Eng-SRE: Filing followups: postmortem, runbook, and monitoring alert for metric gap > 10% between served_tokens and metered_tokens per tenant.
Oliver - Finance: I'll provision the interim credit once Support confirms amount. Please keep me posted.
Emma - Support: Thanks everyone. Closing loop with ACME now and will update ticket TICKET-2026-197 with canary data and next steps. :thumbsup:
billing-bot: Billing export job completed for 2026-02-28 — export id exp_20260228_77 (used by Finance).
Emma - Support: Noted. Will attach export to ticket.
ACME Ops - Customer: Thanks all. Appreciate the quick action and the interim credit offer.
